issues.description: NamespaceSealed stub returns false unconditionally while security-sensitive callers already trust it
issues.detail: Core.NamespaceSealed always returns false with a TODO, yet ListAllNamespaces, root-token paths, and ErrNamespaceSealed handling are wired against it. Shipping a permanently-false security predicate is a regression disguised as a hook. Land SealManager in the same patch, or have the function fail loudly until it exists.

issues.description: ErrNamespaceSealed dispatch uses substring matching on error text instead of errors.Is
issues.detail: AdjustErrorStatusCode uses errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error()), substring-matching 'namespace is sealed' anywhere in any wrapped error. Any handler, plugin, or audit message containing that phrase will be coerced to 503. Errors are values; use errors.Is on the sentinel.

issues.description: Root ACL ancestry semantics changed via HasParent without explicit invariant or full test matrix
issues.detail: AllowOperation gates root on !ns.HasParent(a.root), and NewACL no longer constrains root policies to the root namespace. The reflexivity of HasParent is unstated, and tests only cover happy-path child-ns allow plus root-context deny. Missing: sibling/cousin denial, deep-descendant allow, root-of-root. Latent privilege-escalation risk until the matrix is exhaustively covered and the precondition documented.

issues.description: AllowOperation silently returns empty deny on namespace.FromContext error
issues.detail: The reordered fast-path now does ns, err := namespace.FromContext(ctx); if err != nil { return ret }. An empty ACLResults is indistinguishable from a normal deny — no log, no diagnostic. Missing namespace context silently denies every operation, exactly the kind of silent failure that bites in incident response.

issues.description: ACL.root overloads a nillable *Namespace pointer to mean both is-root and which-namespace
issues.detail: The root field encodes two facts in one sentinel-pointer: nil means 'not root', non-nil means 'root, scoped here'. A small struct{IsRoot bool; NS *Namespace} or named RootScope type would make AllowOperation self-evident and remove the convention the reader must internalize.

issues.description: NSTokenLength built with "."[1] byte-indexing is gratuitously opaque
issues.detail: Encoding the separator length by indexing into a string literal costs reader-seconds for no gain. A named const SeparatorLen = 1, or len("."), expresses intent and survives a separator change. Small, but exactly the kind of cleverness that confuses the next maintainer.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. Three P0s dominate: a NamespaceSealed stub that lies (always false) while security-sensitive callers already depend on it, ErrNamespaceSealed dispatched via substring matching instead of errors.Is, and a root-ACL ancestry semantic shift via HasParent that widens trust without a stated invariant or exhaustive test matrix. Secondary concerns: silent empty-deny on FromContext error, an overloaded ACL.root pointer, and gratuitously clever length arithmetic. Split the ACL change out, land SealManager alongside or fail loudly, and switch sentinel comparison to errors.Is.
